answer: Each identity is granted one coastal ledge and may cut a single shale tablet from that face. The tablet must hang in the ocean through one full tidal cycle so salt and wave wear leave a unique bedding-plane etch. Peers later lift that same tablet from the same ledge and must match the etch to the live tide record. A freshly cut tablet has no valid etch until the cycle ends, and neither the ledge nor the tablet can be shared, so every alias owes its own quarry cut, its own mooring, and a night in the water.
